title: Is a Lapland day trip from the UK worth it?
author: Matt
intro: A Lapland day trip gets you to meet Santa in the snow and home the same night, without paying for hotels. But it's a long, dark day with only a few hours on the ground. Here's what you get, what it costs and when a short break is better.
seo_title: Lapland day trip from the UK: worth it? (2026)
seo_description: Yes, if meeting Santa is the point: about £600 to £830 per person. But you get a few hours on the ground, mostly in the dark. How it compares to a short break.

sections.heading: The short answer
sections.text:
**A Lapland day trip is worth it if the main point is meeting Santa in real snow**, and you'd rather not take time off or pay for three or four nights. It's not worth it if you're hoping for the northern lights, a husky safari through the forest, or a relaxed pace.

The big thing brochures don't stress is the light. In mid-December, Finnish Lapland gets only about two to three hours of daylight. By the time a day trip lands, it's often already getting dark.

sections.heading: Two ways to do it
sections.text:
**1. A charter day trip package.** This is what most people mean by a Lapland day trip. A tour operator charters a plane from a UK regional airport, usually to Rovaniemi or Kittilä. The price includes the flights, transfers, warm clothing, a meal, activities in the snow and a private meeting with Santa.

When we checked in October 2026, December day trips were advertised from about **£600 to £830 per person**, depending on the airport and date. TUI has advertised Santa day trips from 11 regional UK airports, from £750 per person. Some smaller operators run one-off charters from airports like City of Derry.

**2. Do it yourself on normal flights.** EasyJet and Ryanair fly to Rovaniemi from some UK airports in winter, and on the right days you can fly out in the morning and back the same evening. It's much cheaper, but you'll have only about three to four hours in town. You'd also need to organise everything yourself, from transfers to booking a visit to Santa Claus Village.

sections.heading: What the day actually looks like
sections.text:
A typical charter day goes like this:

- **Very early start.** Check-in can be around 6am, for a departure at about 8am.
- **About three and a half hours' flying.** Finland is **two hours ahead of the UK**, so you land in the early afternoon local time.
- **A few hours on the ground.** You change into snowsuits and boots, then go on a short husky or reindeer sleigh ride, play in the snow, have a meal and meet Santa. Time on the ground varies by operator, so check the itinerary.
- **Late return.** You fly home in the evening and land back in the UK late at night.

It's a long day for anyone, especially young children. Most people who enjoy it are fine with that, because it's the single moment with Santa they've come for.

sections.heading: The dark and the cold
sections.text:
Rovaniemi, the main Santa town, sits right on the Arctic Circle. A local guide there puts daylight at about **3 hours 43 minutes on 1 December**, falling to **about 2 hours 14 minutes on the shortest day**. On a day trip landing in the early afternoon, you'll see the end of the twilight and spend most of your time in floodlit snow.

That can be magical, with lights on the snow and deep blue skies. But it means you won't see the forest by daylight, and photos are harder to take.

Average December temperatures are around **-6°C by day and -12°C at night**, and cold snaps can be far colder. Day trip packages lend you thermal suits and boots, but bring thermal underwear, warm socks, hats and mittens of your own.

sections.heading: Day trip or short break?
sections.text:
A three- or four-night break costs much more, and charter short breaks with activities and a Santa visit can cost well over £1,000 per adult. But you get far more for the extra:

- **Northern lights:** your best chance is on dark, clear nights, and you need several nights to give yourself a realistic shot. A day trip gives you almost none.
- **Proper activities:** a longer husky safari, snowmobiling, ice fishing or a night in a glass igloo.
- **A gentler pace:** time to get used to the cold and enjoy it, rather than rushing to the next slot.

If you're deciding where to stay, our post on [Rovaniemi, Levi or Saariselkä](/blog/rovaniemi-levi-or-saariselka) compares the main bases. Our [Tromsø or Rovaniemi](/blog/tromso-or-rovaniemi) post covers the Norwegian alternative.

sections.heading: Tips if you book a day trip
sections.text:
1. **Choose a date before mid-December** if you can. It's usually cheaper, and the days are slightly longer.
2. **Fly from your nearest airport.** The whole point is avoiding a hotel, so a long drive at 4am cancels out the benefit.
3. **Read the itinerary closely.** Check how long you'll spend on the ground, what activities are included and whether the Santa visit is private.
4. **Bring your own layers.** Snowsuits are provided, but thermals and spare gloves make a big difference.
5. **Don't plan on seeing the northern lights.** If you do, treat it as a bonus.

sections.heading: If it's not for you
sections.text:
If a day trip sounds too rushed, consider going in **January to March**, when Lapland is quieter, cheaper and much lighter. Our post on the [quietest time to visit Lapland](/blog/quietest-time-to-visit-lapland) explains when.

Our guides to [Rovaniemi](/destinations/rovaniemi), [Levi](/destinations/levi) and [Saariselkä](/destinations/saariselka) cover each place in detail. For other festive trips, our [Christmas holidays](/destinations/christmas-holidays) page and our guide to [where to go for a white Christmas](/blog/where-to-go-for-a-white-christmas) have more ideas.

If your family can't agree between Lapland and something else entirely, our guide to [how to decide where to go on holiday](/how-to-decide-where-to-go-on-holiday) can help.

faqs.question: How much does a Lapland day trip from the UK cost?
faqs.answer: When we checked in October 2026, December charter day trips were advertised from about £600 to £830 per person, including flights, warm clothing, activities and a meeting with Santa. Doing it yourself on scheduled flights can be cheaper, but you'll have less time.

faqs.question: How long do you get in Lapland on a day trip?
faqs.answer: Usually a few hours. Flights take about three and a half hours each way, and Finland is two hours ahead of the UK. Check your operator's itinerary for the exact time on the ground.

faqs.question: Will you see the northern lights on a Lapland day trip?
faqs.answer: It's unlikely. You need a dark, clear sky with aurora activity, and day trips usually fly home in the evening. A stay of several nights gives a much better chance.

faqs.question: Is it light in Lapland in December?
faqs.answer: Only briefly. Rovaniemi gets about two to three and a half hours of daylight in December, with the shortest day around 21 December.
